newsitem.title: UK: UK government ready to look again at Hillsborough.
newsitem.headline: UK government ready to look again at Hillsborough.

text.p: The British government promised on Tuesday to consider any evidence which threw new light on a 1989 disaster at the Hillsborough stadium in Sheffield in which 96 football fans died.

Home Secretary Michael Howard's pledge followed a demand for the reopening of an inquiry into the tragedy from opposition Labour Party member Peter Kilfoyle, whose constituency includes Anfield, the home of Liverpool football club.
All the 96 fans who died in a crush at the stadium during a match against Sheffield Wednesday were Liverpool supporters.
Relatives of the victims have called for further investigation after the showing of a television drama documentary earlier this month which claimed to uncover new evidence.
Screening of the programme on December 5 revived calls for a new public inquiry into police conduct at Hillsborough and greater compensation for relatives of the dead.
Howard told the House of Commons he had listened carefully to representations from families of victims and from others.
"I must emphasise that I would not take a decision to reopen the inquiry lightly. I must be convinced that it would be in the public interest to do so."
Howard said he would consider carefully the charge that there had been a cover-up and whether there was any new evidence significant enough to alter the outcome of the inquiry.
But he insisted: "New evidence has to be made on the basis of fact, not a TV programme."
Earlier this month, a Liverpool fan won 201,729 pounds ($334,000) in damages from the police for the stress caused by his half-brother's death in the disaster.
